thread_analysis.thread_summary: Alps Alpine (multiple contacts: Shigeyuki Sakai, Shuhei Umeda, Junya Mizuno, DC1 design department) engages Allion (Toshitaka Mochizuki, Itsuo Sakai, Jun Wang, Misumi Sato, lab engineers) for a large, multi-protocol certification project covering the 'UXC10' automotive infotainment module (built for end customer Volvo) spanning roughly September through late October 2025. The visible thread covers Bluetooth RF/RF PHY/IOPT/profile testing (PBAP, MAP, SPP), the DTM/RF PHY test setup and connection-diagram saga, an Enhanced Power Control dispute that escalated to Qualcomm itself questioning the lab's evidence, and an SPP profile test failure ultimately traced to a missing required companion app -- alongside substantial parallel Wi-Fi Alliance (WFA) certification coordination for the same module, which was identified as outside the Bluetooth SIG certification scope and not separately cased.
all_questions_found: Is a combined antenna-plus-cable-loss value acceptable for RF test path loss compensation, and which specific cable's loss value is needed? (see thread_0004_case_01)

Should RF testing proceed treating chipset-capable Enhanced Power Control as non-supported given it's disabled at the firmware level, and should this be confirmed with the OEM as intentional? Later escalated: can the lab substantiate its claim with documentation/log evidence once Qualcomm itself questioned it? (see thread_0004_case_02)
Does a PBAP/MAP/SPP ICS Table discrepancy with the OEM's expectation require full profile retesting, and at what additional cost? (see thread_0004_case_03)

What does the RF PHY DTM Connection Diagram's ambiguous wiring detail mean, and is the customer's submitted diagram actually sufficient for DTM testing? What is the fully confirmed DTM control-path topology? (see thread_0004_case_04)

Why does SPP fail to reproduce a previously-passing result on retest despite matching ICS settings? Root cause found: a required companion app (BlueSPP.apk) was never installed -- and once found, which of the DUT's three labeled USB debug cables should be used to install/run it? (see thread_0004_case_05)

Who is responsible for issuing the export classification document when a sample is transferred from the lab's Japan facility to its Taiwan facility for BLE optional-feature testing? (see thread_0004_case_06)

Can the DUT be physically returned to the customer between RF testing and RF PHY testing so they can apply a configuration update themselves, given they have no version-based way to confirm an update took effect remotely? (see thread_0004_case_07)

Why does the DUT's serial terminal connection fail to reach its expected prompt (TeraTerm), and separately, why does AutomationExplorer's communication check fail even after that's fixed -- is Loopback mode the correct DUT-mode-entry setting, and does the customer's manual even contain a real DTM procedure? (see thread_0004_case_08)

(Out of Bluetooth SIG scope, not separately cased) Extensive parallel Wi-Fi Alliance certification coordination for the same UXC10 module and Volvo OEM relationship, including WFA Model Name/CID consistency requirements, Test Tool selection dependent on OEM-declared Support Functions, a 6GHz-capability CID requiring Return/resubmission, whether WFA testing includes a transmit-power-strength test item, and support for the OEM's WFA operation manual drafting -- these are genuine, well-documented WFA (not Bluetooth SIG) consulting exchanges that could form the basis of a separate WFA-focused case set if that scope were ever requested.

(Administrative, not separately cased) DUT/equipment submission form logistics (combined vs. separate RF/IOPT submission forms), scheduling coordination, RF test sample return scope (full set vs. partial), per-test expected duration estimates, and a brief, undetailed reference to a separate 'DUT startup connection problem' whose substance does not appear in this thread -- routine project administration or out-of-frame content without a generalizable technical lesson captured here.
thread_analysis.key_technical_discussion: The thread's most valuable Bluetooth-specific technical content spans four linked troubleshooting threads: case_08's DTM/RF PHY test setup saga (a hardware current-limit fix for a terminal connection failure, then identifying the customer's manual was pointing at the wrong procedure step and was missing a genuine DTM section entirely); case_04's resulting Connection Diagram clarification, which iterated across several messages to a fully confirmed topology (DUT <-> USB conversion harness <-> PC running QDART <-> RS232/GPIB <-> RF PHY Test System); case_02's Enhanced Power Control dispute, which escalated from a routine firmware-vs-chipset-capability flag into Qualcomm itself demanding documentary proof, which the lab could only answer via precedent and inference rather than direct log evidence; and case_05's SPP retest failure, whose real root cause (a missing required companion app, not ICS or firmware differences) was only discovered when the OEM pointed it out days later -- a clear illustration of why a surface-plausible explanation written before the thread's later messages are read can simply be wrong.
thread_analysis.key_decision_logic: See thread_0004_case_01 through thread_0004_case_08 for case-specific decision logic; the throughline is careful scope/responsibility delineation (test purpose vs. wiring diagram origin, IOPT-only vs. full-profile-retest cost triggers, lab-internal vs. customer-originated export documentation, hardware vs. firmware vs. missing-tooling failure modes) in a complex, multi-party, multi-protocol certification project.
thread_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: See individual case files; the highest-risk items are case_05 (the original root-cause hypothesis -- stale paired-device state or firmware difference -- was plausible but wrong; the actual cause, a missing required companion app, was only found because the OEM's later message was read) and case_02 (the lab's evidence for its Enhanced Power Control claim was precedent-based inference, not direct proof, which could be challenged further).
thread_analysis.consulting_mistake: An internal question forwarded to the customer about the Connection Diagram (case_04) initially confused the customer due to an outdated Excel rendering issue on the lab's own side, requiring a follow-up clarification before the actual substantive issue (wrong diagram type) could be addressed. More substantively: case_05's original write-up (before the full thread was read) proposed stale paired-device state and firmware differences as the likely causes of the SPP retest failure -- both were wrong; the actual cause (a missing required companion app specified in the test guide) was not found until several messages later, prompted by the OEM rather than discovered proactively by the lab.
thread_analysis.consulting_takeaway: In a large multi-protocol certification project spanning Bluetooth, Wi-Fi Alliance, USB, and other certification programs for the same product and OEM relationship, maintain clear scope boundaries between certification programs while still coordinating shared logistics (sample shipment, scheduling) efficiently. Within the Bluetooth-specific workstream: be precise about which test purpose a given customer-submitted document or diagram was created for before assuming it transfers cleanly to a different test requirement; when a profile retest fails to reproduce a prior pass, check the test guide's full tooling prerequisites (companion apps, required installs) before reaching for ICS, firmware, or pairing-state explanations; and when asked to substantiate a claim about chipset behavior to a skeptical OEM or chip vendor, be explicit about the difference between direct evidence and precedent-based inference rather than overstating confidence.
